why: There is no particle type called `minecraft:ghost_face` in the pinned game: the registry `crates/dsl/data/particles-1.21.11.json`, derived from the server jar, holds 115 types and this is not one, so the `particle` command the emitter would write is one the game refuses to load. Validation names the id and the registry's size. It declares no unit: `particle`, both of its `at` forms, `count`, `spread` and `speed` are bound by the hall's case-opening timeline; what the engine refuses here is a name the game does not draw. An id whose type takes options (`minecraft:dust`) is refused by the same code, because the verb carries no options. The remedy is a registered id a bare name spawns — the full-screen face is `minecraft:elder_guardian`.
